research_gap: Whether released generated negative Rego assertions establish a denied decision under an explicitly stated consumer contract, rather than merely succeeding on a defined set-valued expression.
questions: What assertion forms and native outcomes occur in the acquired Rego artifact snapshot under a pinned qualification runtime?
Can a default-allow change produce a source-request decision difference while the unchanged selected negative assertion group passes?
Can separately generated typed assertions reject the demonstrated permissive outcomes under a declared deny-overrides contract?
hypothesis: For some source-informed candidates, bare set-valued deny assertions pass despite allow=true and an empty deny set. Under the authored Boolean-allow/set-deny contract, explicit assertions reject those outcomes.
hypothesis_status: Supported for the conditional tested cases, not for unobserved applications or natural authorization intent
